[Management API](admin-api.html)

The embedded LDAP directory's groups. A group here GRANTS NOTHING: no token, assertion, ticket or PAC carries one and no endpoint reads one.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## GET /admin-api/groups

`getGroups`

**Every group in the embedded LDAP directory, or one in full**

Without `group` it is the list. With it, one group: every attribute it holds, operational ones included, and every member resolved.

Two answers are easy to mistake for failures and are neither. A process with no directory loaded answers 200 with `directory: false`. A group that is not there answers 200 with `found: false`, because a client can delete or rename one through the protocol between one call and the next, and that is the interesting case rather than a routing problem.

A GROUP HERE GRANTS NOTHING, with two exceptions: no endpoint in this service decides anything on a group, and the only two that do are `admin.readGroup` and `admin.writeGroup`, which say who may use the console. A token CAN carry one — `groups.claim` is on by default and puts the subject's groups in every access token, ID Token and SAML assertion — and carrying a fact is not acting on one.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/groups` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | query | string |  | One group's DN. Returns the drill-down. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Substring of the DN or the name, case-insensitive. |
| `exclude` | query | array |  | A group DN to leave out of the match, compared as LDAP compares a DN (case and the spaces after a comma do not matter); repeat it for several. Applied before the paging, so a page still holds `per` rows. Ignored when `group` is given. |
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `membersPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `members` to return, answered by `membersPaging`. The membership values of the group named by `group`, resolved. `group.memberCount`, `presentCount` and `danglingCount` beside them are counts of the WHOLE list and not of the page — a group whose seven members resolve to five is the fact this resource exists to report, and a per-page count would not be an answer to it. |
| `claimedPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `claimed` to return, answered by `claimedPaging`. Entries whose own memberOf names this group while it does not list them back. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## POST /admin-api/groups/add-member

`addGroupMember`

**Put somebody in a group that already exists**

One membership value onto one group. `group` is its `cn` or its whole DN; `member` is a user name or any DN.

**IT IS IDEMPOTENT.** Adding somebody already listed answers `ok: true` with `changed: false` rather than an error, so a script that adds on every run does not fail on its second one. Membership is asked across `member`, `uniqueMember` and `memberUid` together, which is how /admin/groups and the groups claim ask it — an add that could not see a `memberUid` would write a second value for one membership.

**It writes onto `member`** whatever else the entry carries, rather than extending whichever convention the group already uses: this service's groups claim, the console and RFC 4519 all read `member` first, and guessing which of three attributes was meant would be this operation deciding something the caller did not say.

**It does not create the group as a side effect.** A typo in the name would then be a new group rather than an error. And it writes nothing onto the PERSON: `memberOf` is maintained by nothing here — it is not even a standard attribute — and a value written there is one no other door in this service can take away.

**Removing one is not here.** It is an `ldapmodify` or a SCIM `PATCH`, and POST /admin-api/rbac for the two groups that grant the console.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/groups and POST /admin/groups/owners` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/groups/add-owner

`addGroupOwner`

**Add one owner to a group**

Adds a person or a group of this realm to the group's `owner` values (RFC 4519 section 2.23) and writes at once, keeping the other owners. `owner` is a username, a DN or a `urn:uuid:` subject for a person, a `cn` or DN for a group.

**Unlike a member, an owner must name somebody**: one that names no person and no group here is refused. A group may not own itself, and names at most 25 owners. An owner already listed is `ok` with `changed: false`.

**AN OWNER GRANTS NOTHING**: nothing in this service reads `owner` to decide anything.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/groups and POST /admin/groups/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | string | yes | The group's `cn`, DN or SCIM id. |
| `owner` | string | yes | The person or group to add. |

**200**: Whether anything changed, and the group's owners as they now stand (`owners`).

## POST /admin-api/groups/create

`createGroup`

**Put a group in the directory**

An entry under `ou=groups`, as a `groupOfNames` — so it is counted as a group by BOTH of the rules /admin/groups applies, its placement and its object class, and stays one if a client moves it.

**The name becomes the `cn` AND the RDN**, so it is refused if it carries a character RFC 4514 section 2.4 reserves in a DN (one of `, = + < > # ; " \`) — the same rule a username is refused by, and refused rather than escaped for the same reason: an `ldapadd` can still create such an entry with the escaping written out. A DN sent here is refused too, because what it would create is a group whose name is another group's DN.

**A member that names nothing is WRITTEN, not refused.** This directory does no referential integrity in either direction — deleting a person leaves their DN in every group that listed them — so a create that refused a dangling member would make the state /admin/groups exists to report impossible to produce from this door. They come back in `dangling`.

**An empty group is allowed and RFC 4519 says it should not be** (`member` is MUST on `groupOfNames`). SCIM already creates one; a management API stricter than SCIM about the same store would be two doors disagreeing about what this directory holds.

**IT GRANTS NOTHING.** No endpoint here decides anything on a group. The two that do are `admin.readGroup` and `admin.writeGroup`, and they are granted at POST /admin-api/rbac rather than by creating a group with the right name — though creating one with the right name and adding somebody to it does the same thing, because those two ARE ordinary groups in this directory.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/groups and POST /admin/groups/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `displayName` | string |  | Accepted for `group`, spelt the way SCIM spells it. |
| `group` | string | yes | The `cn`. Not a DN — this puts it under `ou=groups` in the realm the call is made in. |
| `mail` | string |  | The group's own email address, its `mail` attribute (#989): where a report definition shared with the group sends its result notices. One address, or omitted. |
| `members` | list, or string |  |  |
| `members[]` | string |  |  |
| `note` | string |  | What the entry's `description` says about why it exists. Defaults to a sentence saying it was created by hand rather than by a directory client. |

**200**: The DN it was created at, the membership values written, and which of them name nothing.

## POST /admin-api/groups/set-mail

`setGroupMail`

**Set or clear a group's email address**

Writes one `mail` value onto the group's own entry, or removes it when `mail` is empty. It is where a report definition shared with the group sends its result notices (the reports application, #989); a shared group with no address is written up as STS-REPORT-0037 when a notice is due. `group` is its `cn` or its whole DN. **Idempotent**: the same address again, or clearing one that is already absent, answers `ok: true` with `changed: false`. A value that is not an address (one local part, one `@`, a domain with a dot, no whitespace) is refused.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/groups and POST /admin/groups/owners` on the admin console.

|---|---|---|---|

## POST /admin-api/groups/set-policy

`setGroupPolicy`

**Set or clear the named policy a group names of one kind**

Writes one value of `attribute` — the attribute by which a group names its policy of a kind, `stsPasskeyPolicy` for the passkey policy — onto the group's own entry, or removes it when `policy` is empty. `policy` is `default` or a named policy of that kind this realm holds (STS-LDAP-0195 otherwise); an attribute no kind declares is refused (STS-LDAP-0194). The policy a group names competes for each of its members on precedence with the policy the application names, the policy the person names and the policies their other groups name: the lowest applies, ties by name, else `default`. A named policy a group still names cannot be deleted. `GET /admin-api/groups?group=` lists the attributes and their choices as `policyReferences`. **Idempotent**: the value the group already names answers `changed: false`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/groups and POST /admin/groups/owners` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attribute` | string | yes | The reference attribute, as `policyReferences` lists it. |
| `group` | string | yes | The group's `cn` or its whole DN. |
| `policy` | string |  | `default`, a named policy of the kind, or empty to remove it. |

**200**: Whether anything changed, and the policy the group now names.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attribute` | string |  |  |
| `changed` | boolean |  |  |
| `dn` | string |  |  |
